You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

{
 "path": "/home/USER/continual-arc-baselines/.workbench/stage1/HPL0-hermes-luna6-high-ws0/frozen/seen/play/users/u078/system/state/workspace/programs/task-96121527.py",
 "content": "from collections import Counter


def _mode(values):
    counts = Counter(values)
    return max(counts, key=lambda v: (counts[v], -v))


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    row_modes = [_mode(row) for row in grid]
    col_modes = [_mode([grid[r][c] for r in range(h)]) for c in range(w)]

    def rare_mode(modes):
        counts = Counter(modes)
        # Lattice lines are the minority row/column class; ties prefer the
        # mode occurring on the more uniform separator lines only as a fallback.
        return min(counts, key=lambda v: (counts[v], v))

    line_color = rare_mode(row_modes)
    rows = [r for r, value in enumerate(row_modes) if value == line_color]
    col_line_color = rare_mode(col_modes)
    cols = [c for c, value in enumerate(col_modes) if value == col_line_color]

    # The separator color is the same in both directions. If row/column
    # classification differs due to sparse markers, use each axis's positions.
    # Intersections not equal to the separator color are the colored corner marks.
    marks = [(ri, ci) for ri, r in enumerate(rows) for ci, c in enumerate(cols)
             if grid[r][c] != line_color]
    if not marks:
        return [[_mode([v for row in grid for v in row])]]

    r0 = min(p[0] for p in marks)
    r1 = max(p[0] for p in marks)
    c0 = min(p[1] for p in marks)
    c1 = max(p[1] for p in marks)
    selected_rows = rows[r0:r1 + 1]
    selected_cols = cols[c0:c1 + 1]

    # The ordinary tile fill is the dominant mode of the non-separator rows.
    interior_modes = [v for v in row_modes if v != line_color]
    fill = _mode(interior_modes) if interior_modes else _mode([v for row in grid for v in row])

    out = []
    for i in range(len(selected_rows) - 1):
        line = []
        for j in range(len(selected_cols) - 1):
            corners = [grid[selected_rows[i]][selected_cols[j]],
                       grid[selected_rows[i]][selected_cols[j + 1]],
                       grid[selected_rows[i + 1]][selected_cols[j]],
                       grid[selected_rows[i + 1]][selected_cols[j + 1]]]
            line.append(corners[0] if corners[0] != line_color and all(x == corners[0] for x in corners) else fill)
        out.append(line)
    return out


if __name__ == '__main__':
    pass
",
 "cross_profile": false
}

 "content": "from collections import Counter


def _mode(values):
    counts = Counter(values)
    return max(counts, key=lambda value: (counts[value], -value))


def _line_positions(modes):
    counts = Counter(modes)
    # Separator lines are the minority row/column mode in these repeating grids.
    line_color = min(counts, key=lambda value: (counts[value], value))
    return line_color, [i for i, value in enumerate(modes) if value == line_color]


def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    row_color, row_candidates = _line_positions([_mode(row) for row in grid])
    col_color, col_candidates = _line_positions(
        [_mode([grid[r][c] for r in range(h)]) for c in range(w)]
    )

    # Keep only lattice lines that participate in a colored intersection. This
    # removes unmarked outer padding/borders from the encoded rectangle.
    line_color = row_color
    rows = [r for r in row_candidates
            if any(grid[r][c] != line_color for c in col_candidates)]
    cols = [c for c in col_candidates
            if any(grid[r][c] != line_color for r in rows)]

    if len(rows) < 2 or len(cols) < 2:
        return [[_mode([v for row in grid for v in row])]]

    # The ordinary tile color fills any rectangle whose four lattice corners
    # do not all carry the same marker color.
    interior = [grid[r][c] for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
                if r not in row_candidates and c not in col_candidates]
    fill = _mode(interior) if interior else _mode([v for row in grid for v in row])

    output = []
    for i in range(len(rows) - 1):
        out_row = []
        for j in range(len(cols) - 1):
            corners = (grid[rows[i]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i]][cols[j + 1]],
                       grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j]], grid[rows[i + 1]][cols[j + 1]])
            color = corners[0]
            out_row.append(color if color != line_color and all(x == color for x in corners) else fill)
        output.append(out_row)
    return output


if __name__ == '__main__':
    pass
